page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-192 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs derived from 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 1488 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core performance, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. The CPU features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to strong performance in specialized tasks such as software compilation and LLM inference processing. However, single-core performance, as measured by stress-ng single-core tests, falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 573.67 GB/sec for large block read-only operations, though the overall Passmark memory score remains in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a high-capacity memory profile paired with massive parallel compute capabilities, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The lack of bundled local storage means storage-heavy operations must rely on network-attached volumes. This server is highly suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, multi-threaded software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
